member.name: DocIncludedText.Compose
member.summary: D.3.6 — a summary that exists only in this file. The declaration it documents has no <summary> of its own: its documentation comment is a single <include> tag, and the compiler replaces that tag with these children when it writes Docs.xml. An index reading the syntax tree sees the tag; an index reading the documentation file sees this. The two disagree, and which one answers is the fact.
member.returns: D.3.6 — the composed text, described from outside the source file.

member.name: DocIncludedText.Lines
member.summary: D.3.6 — a second member, selected by a different XPath predicate.
member.remarks: D.3.6 — path selects the member element's children, so this <remarks> and the summary above both land on the declaration.
member.returns: D.3.6 — how many lines were composed.
